apple.price_source: apple.com/de store: embedded product data of the /de/shop/buy-mac/<family> pages plus the store's own configurator API (/de/shop/api/cto/update-config), fetched 2026-11-15. All prices EUR incl. VAT.
apple.core_fields: Apple now names three core classes (Super / Performance / Effizienz). perf_cores = Super + Performance cores, eff_cores = Effizienz cores; super_cores is given separately where Apple states it. For M5 Pro/Max/Ultra Apple lists no efficiency cores at all.
apple.benchmark_source: Geekbench 6 Mac Benchmark Chart (https://browser.geekbench.com/mac-benchmarks, tabs Single-Core / Multi-Core / Metal), read 2026-11-15. Each chip uses the scores of the one Mac model named in ref_model.

devices.linux_support: Framework sells the DIY Edition without an OS and states on the configurator 'bringen Sie Ihr Betriebssystem mit, auch Linux'.
devices.note: Read 2026-11-15. DIY system prices without RAM/SSD are 959 / 1269 / 1679 EUR (sale, 'Vorher' 1059 EUR for the 340); base_price here = system + cheapest RAM kit (8 GB, +179) + cheapest SSD (500 GB SN7100, +150), 2.2K display, no OS, no power adapter/expansion cards. RAM steps use the cheapest kit per capacity (16 GB = 1x16 +305, 32 GB = 1x32 +575, 64 GB = 2x32 +1150); 8 TB is the SANDISK 850X. The model header showed an 'Out of stock' badge next to the generation tabs, so availability of this non-Pro model is uncertain.

open_points: apple: Mac Pro: https://www.apple.com/de/shop/buy-mac/mac-pro and https://www.apple.com/de/mac-pro/ both redirect to the Mac overview, which no longer lists a Mac Pro - treated as not sold, no device entry.

apple: MacBook Air 13: the 1509 EUR for M5 10-GPU with 16 GB/512 GB is the store's 'Ab' price for that chip and was cross-checked only indirectly (configurator total 1923.99 EUR = 1509 + Final Cut Pro 349.99 + 35 W adapter 65); a direct quote of that bare configuration could not be pulled from the API.

apple: RAM/SSD surcharges are the configurator's price deltas for options that keep the same chip; sizes that force a chip change (e.g. 36/128 GB on M5 Pro, 8 TB on M5 Pro, 48+ GB on Mac mini M6) are deliberately left out of that variant's lists.

apple: fanless=false for MacBook Pro, Mac mini, iMac and Mac Studio is not stated explicitly on apple.com/de (only the Mac mini spec page mentions its thermal system); fanless=true is confirmed by Apple for MacBook Air (product page) and MacBook Neo (Newsroom DE).
apple: Education prices and the nano-texture / stand / Ethernet options were not captured.
apple: MacBook Neo: store price today (799 / 899 EUR) is higher than the Newsroom DE launch price (ab 699 EUR, March 2026); the date and reason of the change were not researched.
apple: Geekbench: scores are per Mac model, not per chip; one reference model per chip was chosen (see ref_model). No Metal score exists in the chart for the iMac M6 10-core (gpu null).
apple: Geekbench: the chart does not separate GPU-core variants for M1 Max (24/32) and M2 (8/10); gpu_cores is null there.

apple: Intel i9-9880H: Geekbench has no per-Mac Metal row; gpu uses the Radeon Pro 5500M value from the Metal chart on the assumption that this was the standard GPU of the 2.3 GHz i9 configuration (5300M would be 33130) - not verified against an Apple source.

apple: Core splits of the older comparison chips (M1 to M4 families) come from Apple's compare page where listed (M1, M2, M3, M4, M1 Pro 10c, M1 Max, M2 Pro 12c, M2 Max, M3 Max 16c, M4 Pro 14c, M4 Max 16c); the lower sub-variants (M1 Pro 8c, M2 Pro 10c, M3 Pro 11c/12c, M3 Max 14c, M4 Pro 12c, M4 Max 14c) are from Apple's historic specs as remembered, not re-verified today.
apple: Extra fields beyond the requested schema: top-level 'meta', chip fields 'super_cores' and 'ref_model', and variant field 'released' on macbook-pro-14.

linux: GPU scores are Geekbench 6 OpenCL; they are only roughly comparable with Geekbench 6 Metal scores of Apple chips (different API and drivers), and Geekbench lists several differently named entries per GPU (e.g. Radeon 8060S: 86120 as 'AMD Radeon(TM) 8060S Graphics' but 91472, 83568 and 78546 under other driver strings; Radeon 780M: 21347, 24388, 25072) - the Windows-driver-named entry was used.

linux: All prices were read on 2026-11-15 during a DRAM shortage and are volatile (Framework charges +610 EUR for 2x16 GB DDR5; Strix Halo 128 GB mini PCs cost 3350-4600 EUR; Raspberry Pi 5 16 GB about 390-416 EUR).

linux: No Geekbench 6 chart entry (browser.geekbench.com/processor-benchmarks, 827 CPUs) existed for: Ryzen 7 H 255, Ryzen AI 5 PRO 440, Ryzen AI 7 PRO 450, Ryzen AI 7 445, Ryzen 5 PRO 224, Ryzen 5 PRO 216, Ryzen AI Max+ 495 / PRO 495, Core Ultra 5 325, Core Ultra 7 356H, Core Ultra X7 358H, Core Ultra X9 388H, Broadcom BCM2712 - single/multi are null.

linux: iGPU assignment for chips marked verified=false is from secondary sources (notebookcheck: PRO 450 -> Radeon 860M, PRO 440 and AI 7 445 -> Radeon 840M; X7 358H/X9 388H -> Arc B390 with 12 Xe cores) and the GPU score is the chart value of that GPU; the Ryzen 7 H 255 -> Radeon 780M mapping is from the TUXEDO shop text. No GPU score was assigned to Core Ultra 5 325, Core Ultra 7 356H, Ryzen AI Max+ 495 (a 'Radeon 8065S' entry with OpenCL 96202 exists but was not mapped), Ryzen 5/7 PRO 2xx or the Raspberry Pi (no usable OpenCL/Vulkan entry).

linux: Core counts: Framework and TUXEDO pages give only totals for AMD chips, so all cores are in perf_cores and eff_cores=0; the Zen 5 / Zen 5c split (reported by secondary sources as 4+8 for HX 370, 4+4 for AI 7 350 / PRO 450, 3+3 for AI 5 340 / PRO 440, 2+4 for AI 7 445) is not broken out. Core counts for Ryzen AI 7 445, AI 5 PRO 440, AI 7 PRO 450 and Core Ultra 7 356H come from secondary sources; Ryzen 5 PRO 224/216, Ryzen 7 PRO 250, Ryzen AI Max+ 495 (non-PRO) and BCM2712 were not read and are null. For Intel Series 3, eff_cores = E-cores + LP E-cores (X7/X9: 8+4; Ultra 5 325: 0+4).

linux: Release months are null wherever no page read in this session stated them (Framework Laptop 13/16/Desktop, both TUXEDO models, ThinkPad T14/X1 Carbon/P14s, Beelink models); the given ones are secondary (Framework 13 Pro announcement 2026-04, T14s Gen 7 2026-04, Pi 5 16 GB 2025-01) or a store listing date (GMKtec EVO-X2 2025-05).

linux: Lenovo: only ready-made Windows models of lenovo.com/de were readable; configure-to-order RAM/SSD surcharges and a Linux/no-OS option could not be read, and Ubuntu / Red Hat certification of the 2026 generations (T14 Gen 7, T14s Gen 7, X1 Carbon Gen 14, P14s Gen 7, P16s Gen 5) was not checked against ubuntu.com/certified or the Red Hat catalogue. Lenovo web prices are temporary discount prices.

linux: Framework DIY base prices are composed (system + cheapest RAM + cheapest SSD) because the DIY edition is sold without both; power adapter, expansion cards, Laptop 16 input modules and Framework Desktop fan/tiles/power cable are not included. Framework Desktop 300-series SSD surcharges were not opened on its own configurator and are taken from the identical list on the PRO 400 and laptop configurators.
linux: Display sizes: Framework Laptop 13 Pro (both) not read (null); Framework Laptop 16 and both TUXEDO models are taken from the model name, the InfinityBook Max 15 diagonal is not confirmed.

linux: Mini-PC prices (Beelink, GMKtec) come from the stores' own Shopify product feeds (products.json, shop currency EUR verified via cart.js), not from the rendered product page; checkout price, VAT display and shipping were not verified. GMKtec EVO-X2 has no documented vendor Linux support.

linux: Raspberry Pi 5 16 GB kit: reseller price only (verified=false), not deliverable on 2026-11-15, kit contents unknown; the originally linked BerryBase 'Starterkit 64GB microSDHC' 16 GB page returned 'Seite nicht gefunden'.

linux: Not covered: Slimbook, Minisforum (MS-S1 MAX 128 GB/2 TB was 4319 EUR, UM880 Plus Ryzen 7 8845HS 16 GB/512 GB 739 EUR in the store.minisforum.de feed), ThinkPad T14 Gen 7 Intel, P16s with discrete GPU, Framework pre-built editions (except the Desktop PRO 495 price in the note).
